chunks: What the Shaykh — may Allah, Exalted is He, support him — informed me of, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ṣafwān, from Manṣūr, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about one who forgot to wipe his head until he had stood in the salat (prayer). He said: “He should turn away and wipe his head and his feet.”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the salat (prayer) in which he had already stood
key_terms.رَأْسَهُ: his head, whose wiping is required in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.رِجْلَيْهِ: his feet, which are to be wiped in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.يَمْسَحَ: to wipe as part of wudu (ablution)
key_terms.يَنْصَرِفُ: he should leave or turn away from the prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he forgot to wipe his head in wudu (ablution) until after standing in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding one who omitted wiping the head during wudu (ablution) and only remembered after standing in salat (prayer). Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام instructs that he must leave the prayer and complete the required wiping of the head and feet, showing the necessity of proper ritual purity for valid prayer.
